channel.title: IndieHOT — Indie Game Hot Topics
channel.description: IndieHOT collects indie game news from a set of public sources every day and scores it by rules: engines & tools, publishing & marketing, devlogs, industry & funding, events, reviews & postmortems. Only titles, one-line self-written summaries and outbound links are shown — no full text is republished.

item.title: Why Your Game VO Always Sounds "Off" — And It's Not the Actors
item.description: Uneven game voiceover is usually a loudness problem, not a performance one — the piece explains how aligning every line to the same LUFS and true-peak targets fixes it.

item.title: # AI Agents in Unity XR Development: From Writing Code to Testing VR Workflows
item.description: From a Meta Quest 3 developer's perspective, the author looks at how AI tools are moving beyond code suggestions toward workflows that interact with development tools — especially valuable for XR, where debugging goes beyond fixing a script.

item.title: Dev snapshot: Godot 4.8 beta 4
item.description: Godot 4.8 is nearing release, with beta 4 clearing most remaining release blockers and possibly being the last beta snapshot of the cycle.

item.title: Engineering the 212 GB Launch: How GTA 6 Redefines Real-Time Asset Streaming and Console Performance
item.description: Starting from the 212 GB install size, it breaks down how GTA 6 uses direct-storage decompression and streaming budgets to eliminate open-world loading screens, and how ray-traced global illumination trades off against frame rate.

item.title: Inside GTA 6: Engine Architecture, PSSR Upscaling, and PS5 Pro Performance
item.description: Starting from a natively captured 4K playthrough on PS5 Pro, this walkthrough breaks down GTA 6's engine tech, from PSSR machine-learning upscaling and real-time ray-traced global illumination to asynchronous world simulation.

item.title: Write Your First Python Battle in 30 Lines (No Experience Needed)
item.description: Build a tiny turn-based battle in 30 lines of Python — a more memorable first project than temperature converters and shopping lists.

item.title: Idlewild: Turn Your Breath into Animation and Sound
item.description: A desktop performance studio for animators and game makers that turns breath into animation and sound in real time — worth a look for developers exploring breath-based interaction.

item.title: Kanto Tactics Beginner Guide: Skip the Guesswork
item.description: A beginner's guide to the browser autobattler Kanto Tactics, covering gold economy, when to merge units, and gym order, plus a free companion reference site — useful reading for developers building similar casual competitive web games.

item.title: Data digest: Pixel Flow, Monster Hunter, October’s top games, Nintendo numbers, more
item.description: This week's mobile data digest covers Pixel Flow, Monster Hunter, October's top games and Nintendo's numbers, plus business updates from Liftoff and other publishers.

item.title: Stylized Roguelite Developer Shares Three Unusual Game Optimization Tricks
item.description: The developers of Barrow and Blade share three unconventional tricks for squeezing performance out of their stylized roguelite.

item.title: Best animation library for Unity UI Toolkit: Cascade vs PrimeTween vs LitMotion
item.description: All three libraries can fade and move UI elements, but they were built for different jobs; the author tested them side by side in one Unity 6000.4 project to guide the choice.

item.title: Unity acquires Synty Studios to bring its asset library to Unity Spark
item.description: Unity has acquired Synty Studios, maker of the Polygon range of stylised 3D packs, bringing more than 60,000 low-poly assets into its AI-native creation platform Unity Spark.

item.title: Pixel Art for a Game Jam: My 16x16 Coin Sprite Sheet Workflow
item.description: The author turns a two-hour struggle with one spinning coin at a game jam into a complete workflow for a 16x16, four-frame coin sprite sheet that plays crisply in Phaser.

item.title: Create Beautiful Stylized Water Easily With This Godot Tool
item.description: This Godot water tool bundles Gerstner waves, shoreline foam, caustics, reflections and waterfalls to help developers build stylized water quickly.

item.title: How to playtest your first video game
item.description: Unity's beginner guide explains what playtesting is, why it matters, and how to run a session and act on feedback while building with AI.

item.title: HTML5 Game Development Cost in 2026: A Buyer's Guide
item.description: A simple casual browser game runs about $3,000–$15,000, while a branded campaign game with custom art and a leaderboard costs $10,000–$40,000 — a useful anchor for budgeting outsourced work.

item.title: Godot's New Sponsor – Manus AI
item.description: Manus AI has joined the Godot Foundation as a platinum-level sponsor — AI companies backing open-source projects is nothing new, but it remains a topic that matters to the community.

item.title: GTA 6 Leads The Game Awards 2026 Nominees With 8 Nods Before Launch: Key Craft & Gamedev Takeaways
item.description: GTA 6 leads The Game Awards 2026 nominees with 8 nods before launch, and this piece pulls out the craft and gamedev lessons worth noting.

item.title: Splitting an Unreal Engine Project Across Two Time Zones: A Handoff Checklist for Offshore Teams
item.description: When a team spans Bengaluru and London or Austin, the working day overlaps for only a few hours, so this checklist turns handoffs into a written routine that keeps the project moving.

item.title: NVIDIA Expands RTX Spark Lineup With Compact Desktops for Developers, Creators, and AI Enthusiasts
item.description: NVIDIA's new compact RTX Spark desktops from ASUS, Dell and MSI pack up to 128GB of unified memory for 3D, video and local AI work.
